clue.text: It's prepared during social event in space

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit during, i.e. within the span of, the dance

parts.note: a dance is a social event

indicators.note: letters that are prepared have been worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something gets got ready while a party happens somewhere roomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' looks like part of the sentence but is the anagram fodder for 'prepared'; 'during' places the result inside the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the space or gap between two points.

clue.text: Monster depriving old horseman of oxygen

indicators.note: depriving the horseman of something means removing it from the word

parts.note: a dragoon was a mounted soldier of old
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A beast robs a cavalryman of his air.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fire-breathing beast of legend, a mythical monster.

clue.text: Leave the outskirts of Seville with upper-class twit

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: a toff is a disparaging British term for a posh person

explanation.surface: Departing the edge of a Spanish city alongside a posh fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to depart, start out on a journey.

clue.text: Everyone at university about to appeal

parts.note: all means everyone
re means about, concerning, as in letters

explanation.surface: The whole college is about to launch an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness or charm, the appeal something has.

clue.text: Capital trick involving hen being changed into paper leaf

indicators.note: the trick word surrounds, i.e. involves, everything else

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the page

parts.note: a page is one leaf of paper in a book

indicators.note: a changed word has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fraud in the city turns a chicken into a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the definition, not money. There are two nested insertions: 'being changed' shuffles the hen, 'into' sets it in the page, and 'involving' wraps the trick round everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen is the capital city of Denmark.

clue.text: Setter's role is to communicate

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so 'setter's' (setter is) gives I'M
an actor's part is their role

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler muses that the job is all about getting a message across.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword convention: 'setter' stands for the first person, so 'Setter's' is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on, a synonym of communicate.

clue.text: Prepared to go round a bottomless piece of ice that's steep

indicators.note: the outer word goes round, enclosing the rest

parts.note: made means prepared

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: a rink is a stretch of ice for skating

explanation.surface: Something ready wraps round a chunk of ice with its base gone, on a steep slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' is the verb, to soak, not the adjective. 'bottomless' works because this is a down entry, so the last letter is the bottom; 'to go round' wraps RIN and A in the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinade food is to steep it in a seasoned liquid before cooking.

clue.text: Newborn adopted by holy man rejected as strange

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are taken in, adopted, by the reversed word
rejected means turned back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

indicators.note: new makes the letters a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A baby is taken in by a monk yet spurned as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newborn' splits in two: 'New' shuffles the letters of 'born' to BNOR, while 'rejected' turns the monk round to AMAL so that 'adopted by' can hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means deviating from the usual, hence odd or strange.

clue.text: Unlawful occupation of locked resort?

indicators.note: read cryptically, 'of locked resort' pictures the resort held within the lock, so 'of' marks one word sitting inside the other

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress; 'locked' points to the lock that holds the resort
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Squatting at a holiday spot that was shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: The envelope is only implied: 'locked resort' pictures a resort (SPA) held in a lock of hair (TRESS), and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is entering or remaining on land without the owner's permission.

clue.text: Ruminant and insect run away to get married

parts.note: an ant is an insect
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: An odd couple, a grazing beast and a bug, dash off to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes chew the cud, so they are ruminants, like cattle and deer.

clue.text: Royal runs off, allegedly

indicators.note: what is alleged is only said, so the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to run off copies is to print them, so 'runs off' gives PRINTS

explanation.surface: Supposedly a member of the royal family has bolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' looks like fleeing but means printing copies; PRINTS said out loud matches PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a son or close male relative of a monarch, hence a royal.

clue.text: Sacrifice bad English jewellery

parts.note: milk that has gone bad is off
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a tacky piece of English jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given to a god, the same idea as a sacrifice.

clue.text: Spouse detailed to return with catch

indicators.note: returning sends the shortened word back the other way
de-tailed: losing its tail, i.e. the final letter

parts.note: a spouse is a partner

explanation.surface: A husband or wife is sent back with something caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' drops the last letter of PARTNER to leave PARTNE, and 'to return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or catch them out.

clue.text: Mistress in a chateau having friendly talk with girl

parts.note: a chat is an informal friendly talk
Elaine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The lady of the castle is chatting with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large house or castle.

clue.text: Assorted charts lead to places of worship

indicators.note: assorted things are mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Following a mix of maps brings you to churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a bishop's principal church, a large place of Christian worship.

clue.text: Culprit placed old farthing on part of fireplace

indicators.note: in a down entry, placing one piece on another puts it above

parts.note: F was the abbreviation for the farthing, an old British quarter-penny coin
a fender is the low guard in front of a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone guilty left an antique coin on the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was a pre-decimal British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a wrongdoer, the culprit of a crime.

clue.text: Instructed to include seal to prevent entry

indicators.note: the first word includes, i.e. contains, the second

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to instruct
to lock something is to seal it

explanation.surface: Orders to seal a door so no one can get in.
explanation.definitionFit: To blockade a place is to cut it off so nothing can get in or out.

clue.text: Gnome set out to find precious rock

indicators.note: out signals letters set out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden gnome sets out in search of a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone is a precious or semi-precious stone cut for jewellery.

clue.text: Butcher left these with a set of choppers

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so these letters are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A meat-cutter abandoned these along with a set of cleavers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' is a verb here, not the shopkeeper, and 'choppers' is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is informal for teeth, so a set of artificial ones is dentures.

clue.text: Despot's extremely tetchy outburst

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a rant is an angry outburst

explanation.surface: A dictator's very irritable tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'tetchy', not the sense 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel absolute ruler, a despot.

clue.text: One may carry drink

explanation.definitionFit: A porter is a baggage carrier, and also a dark brown beer like stout.

clue.text: Article represented a patron saint

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to draw something is to represent it in a picture

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece depicted a country's guardian saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Cut out tax

definitions.meaning: to remove by cutting, as a surgeon does
a duty charged on goods such as alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: Excise is both the verb meaning cut away and the noun for a duty levied on goods.

clue.text: Make light of not working after performance

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: a play is a theatrical performance
a computer system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Shrugging off a broken-down show after the curtain falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To play down a problem is to minimise it, treating it as unimportant.

clue.text: Clergyman keeping company with another

indicators.note: the dean keeps, i.e. holds within, the company abbreviation

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A churchman spends time in the company of a fellow cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'another', meaning another clergyman, since the clue opens with 'Clergyman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister, so it is a second clergyman alongside the dean.

clue.text: New star dies in accident

indicators.note: a new version is a reworked one, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A freshly formed sun perishes in some cosmic mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamitous accident or catastrophe.

clue.text: Leftie eating endless leeks smelt awful

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the inner letters

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

indicators.note: with no ends: the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: A socialist chomping on leeks gives off a terrible odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leftie' is a political red, not a left-hander; 'endless' trims both ends of 'leeks', and 'eating' puts what remains inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeked means stank, giving off a strong unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Passion leading to hot dispute in airport

parts.note: the heat of the moment is passion
H for hot, as marked on taps
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Tempers flare into a heated argument at the terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is the principal airport serving London.
